From ebe560ea5f54134279356703e73b7f867c89db13 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alice Mikityanska <alice@isovalent.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 20:49:49 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] l2tp: Drop large packets with UDP encap

syzbot reported a WARN on my patch series [1]. The actual issue is an
overflow of 16-bit UDP length field, and it exists in the upstream code.
My series added a debug WARN with an overflow check that exposed the
issue, that's why syzbot tripped on my patches, rather than on upstream
code.

syzbot's repro:

r0 = socket$pppl2tp(0x18, 0x1, 0x1)
r1 = socket$inet6_udp(0xa, 0x2, 0x0)
connect$inet6(r1, &(0x7f00000000c0)={0xa, 0x0, 0x0, @loopback, 0xfffffffc}, 0x1c)
connect$pppl2tp(r0, &(0x7f0000000240)=@pppol2tpin6={0x18, 0x1, {0x0, r1, 0x4, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, {0xa, 0x4e22, 0xffff, @ipv4={'\x00', '\xff\xff', @empty}}}}, 0x32)
writev(r0, &(0x7f0000000080)=[{&(0x7f0000000000)="ee", 0x34000}], 0x1)

It basically sends an oversized (0x34000 bytes) PPPoL2TP packet with UDP
encapsulation, and l2tp_xmit_core doesn't check for overflows when it
assigns the UDP length field. The value gets trimmed to 16 bites.

Add an overflow check that drops oversized packets and avoids sending
packets with trimmed UDP length to the wire.

Fixes: 3557baabf280 ("[L2TP]: PPP over L2TP driver core")
Reported-by: syzbot+ci3edea60a44225dec@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/69a1dfba.050a0220.3a55be.0026.GAE@google.com/
Signed-off-by: Alice Mikityanska <alice@isovalent.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260403174949.843941-1-alice.kernel@fastmail.im
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c b/net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c
index c89ae52764b8..157fc23ce4e1 100644
--- a/net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c
+++ b/net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c
@@ -1290,6 +1290,11 @@ static int l2tp_xmit_core(struct l2tp_session *session, struct sk_buff *skb, uns
 		uh->source = inet->inet_sport;
 		uh->dest = inet->inet_dport;
 		udp_len = uhlen + session->hdr_len + data_len;
+		if (udp_len > U16_MAX) {
+			kfree_skb(skb);
+			ret = NET_XMIT_DROP;
+			goto out_unlock;
+		}
 		uh->len = htons(udp_len);
 
 		/* Calculate UDP checksum if configured to do so */
-- 
2.34.1

The patch consists of a single change in one file: `net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c`.

### Modifications in each file

**`net/l2tp/l2tp_core.c`**  
- Added a check inside `l2tp_xmit_core()` after computing `udp_len` (the total UDP payload length).  
- If `udp_len` exceeds `U16_MAX` (65535), the packet is dropped with `kfree_skb(skb)`, the return code is set to `NET_XMIT_DROP`, and execution jumps to the `out_unlock` label.  
- This prevents the subsequent assignment `uh->len = htons(udp_len)` from truncating a too-large value to 16 bits, which would generate a malformed packet and could trigger a kernel warning (as seen in the syzbot report).

### Relationships between modifications

The change is self-contained within a single function. The added overflow check directly addresses the root cause of the bug: the 16‑bit UDP length field overflow when an oversized packet is sent via L2TP over UDP encapsulation. By dropping such packets early, the patch avoids both the incorrect packet generation and the associated warning that was previously exposed by the developer’s debug patches. No other files or dependencies are involved.
